body:
I think `code` adds itself to `$PATH`. Would setting `$EDITOR` to `code` work for you? (BTW I think `code --wait` usually works better when programs like git need to wait for input)

As for not handling spaces, it might be possible to take the longest existing path as a heuristic to separate between arguments and paths, but that's still brittle. I think at least not finding the selected `$EDITOR` could be handled a bit better.

> I think code adds itself to $PATH.

It does but I try to always put whole path in my environment variables. Sometimes I have several executable of the same name in my $PATH.

> Would setting $EDITOR to code work for you?

Nope.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11684337/90336567-f8e86380-dfdc-11ea-8d06-50aa404b4440.png)

But I can't think of a reason why starship wouldn't inherit the env from the shell. I often call `code` by hand.

Edit: it does inherit correctly the environment. The Path is correctly set. It still can't find `code`.

![2020-08-16 (2)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11684337/90336518-aad36000-dfdc-11ea-8bfa-bb7bc97abb08.png)

I cooked that up quickly, but there's another problem here underlying the whole thing.

Edit 2: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11684337/90336803-95f7cc00-dfde-11ea-9590-88ee985402d7.png)

I don't understand the _real_ issue.
Does it work when you add `.exe` to the editor path?

`code` is an sh script without extension (check in `%LocalAppData%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin`).

I also checked by using `code.cmd` explicitely. But it doesn't make difference. Windows should invoke `code.cmd` first when calling `code` already (check by using `Get-Command code`).

Edit: but by using the full path **and** `code.cmd` it works.

<details>
    <summary>transcript of the debug, not much interest</summary>

```
starship on  fix-spaces-in-editor is 📦 v0.44.0 via 🦀 v1.45.2
❯ $env:EDITOR = "C:\Users\jacqu\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin\code.cmd"

starship on  fix-spaces-in-editor is 📦 v0.44.0 via 🦀 v1.45.2
❯ .\target\debug\starship.exe config
[src\configure.rs:68] path_vscode = Ok(
    Some(
        "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft VS Code\\bin",
    ),
)
[src\configure.rs:69] get_config_path() = "C:\\Users\\jacqu\\.config\\starship.toml"
[src\configure.rs:70] get_editor() = (
    "C:\\Users\\jacqu\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Microsoft VS Code\\bin\\code.cmd",
    [],
)
```
and it opens vscode !
</details>

What I find strange here:

1. I can't be the first one to use a full path? with spaces in it? can I?
2. There must be other people who set their editor to `code` on Windows?
3. So if it works for them to simply have `EDITOR=code`, it should work for me, and Windows should do its job and call `code.cmd` regardless.
4. Something on my machine doesn't seem right? Maybe?
5. The parsing of the $EDITOR variable should definitely be improved in starship, it's a pain but there are definitely cases where it breaks currently:
    - spaces in path `/path/to my/vim` (i "fixed" that quickly here, but it's ugly and doesn't work if there are more than one space at a given place)
    - spaces in argument given to options `vim --option="foo bar"` (this requires quote matching and some "real" parsing)
    - other cases I thought about and forgot while eating because I didn't write them down

BTW: I looked at some crates (scrawl, default-editor, open_in_editor) claiming to allow using the EDITOR more easily, they all make the same mistakes. This [one](https://github.com/milkey-mouse/edit/blob/master/src/lib.rs#L84-L110) seems promising but, like my quick hack, misses the cases of spaces in arguments and spaces in the editor path. 

Edit: there is a way to _bypass_ all that work,

```rust
Command::new("bash")
   .arg("-c")
   .arg(format!("$EDITOR {}", config_path))
```

This way all of the actual work is delegated to bash. The same can be done for Windows, but my shell-fu on Windows is lacking/rusty. With some conditional compilation it would be quite easy to have one Unix function and one Windows function.

[Playground](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2018&gist=57b2047592e29ec7bd0c6528ba1201cd), this handles all cases (full path or not, spaces in paths or not) except when the EDITOR is `vi -flag`, but as I learned today, every standard tool also do not accept flags in this variable. The recommended practice is to write a thin wrapper script and set that script as the editor.

Edit: https://lib.rs/crates/shell-words this seems like the more complete approach. I'll try it this afternoon.

<details>
    <summary>Git itself is victim of those issues.</summary>

```
$ EDITOR="/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim -m" git commit --allow-empty
hint: Waiting for your editor to close the file... /tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim -m: 1: /tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim -m: /tmp/testing/spaces: not found
error: There was a problem with the editor '/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim -m'.
Please supply the message using either -m or -F option.
$ EDITOR="'/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim' -m" git commit --allow-empty # works, -m prevents writing as intended
```

quick crate using shell-words

```rust
fn main() {
    let _ = dbg!(shell_words::split(&std::env::var("EDITOR").unwrap()));
}
```

```
$ EDITOR="/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim" cargo run --quiet
[src/main.rs:2] shell_words::split(&std::env::var("EDITOR").unwrap()) = Ok(
    [
        "/tmp/testing/spaces",
        "in",
        "dir/nvim",
    ],
)
$ EDITOR='nvim -m="some option"' cargo run --quiet
[src/main.rs:2] shell_words::split(&std::env::var("EDITOR").unwrap()) = Ok(
    [
        "nvim",
        "-m=some option",
    ],
)
$ EDITOR="'/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim' -m='some option'" cargo run --quiet
[src/main.rs:2] shell_words::split(&std::env::var("EDITOR").unwrap()) = Ok(
    [
        "/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim",
        "-m=some option",
    ],
)
```
Using shell-words -> falling victim to the same issue as git, but better arg parsing.
</details>

<details>
    <summary>Solution: with quoted environment variable</summary>

```rust
fn main() {
    let editor_cmd = dbg!(shell_words::split(&std::env::var("EDITOR").unwrap())).unwrap();
    std::process::Command::new(&editor_cmd[0])
        .args(&editor_cmd[1..])
        .spawn()
        .unwrap()
        .wait()
        .unwrap();
}
```
shell

```
$ EDITOR="'/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim' -m" cargo run --quiet
[src/main.rs:2] shell_words::split(&std::env::var("EDITOR").unwrap()) = Ok(
    [
        "/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim",
        "-m",
    ],
)
$ cargo run --quiet
[src/main.rs:2] shell_words::split(&std::env::var("EDITOR").unwrap()) = Ok(
    [
        "/usr/bin/nvim",
    ],
)
$ EDITOR="'/tmp/testing/spaces in dir/nvim' -m" git commit --allow-empty
Aborting commit due to empty commit message.
```
Launches nvim in read-only correctly and nvim without flag correctly. Git correctly parses the partiallay quoted $EDITOR.
I think it's acceptable for starship to have the same flaws as git?

Checking on windows (same source code), note the single quotes:
```
❯ $env:EDITOR = "'C:\Users\jacqu\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin\code.cmd'"
❯ cargo run --quiet
[src\main.rs:2] shell_words::split(&std::env::var("EDITOR").unwrap()) = Ok(
    [
        "C:\\Users\\jacqu\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Microsoft VS Code\\bin\\code.cmd",
    ],
)
```
VSCode is launched.

</details>

Solution:

- I quoted the whole path to my editor `"%LocalAppData%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin\code.cmd"`.
- Submitted PR to improve (not simply split by whitespace) the parsing of $EDITOR (tested PR on both Windows and Linux as shown here).
